note: A4 dispatcher exam (2026-09-04). train = cases you may iterate the prompt against; heldout = reported score. Never tune on heldout. Split proposed by the build, ratified by the operator at merge (Heldout is untouchable).
not_verified: The label half is exact-match on 'agent' only. The hand-over half is graded by properties.py: the input must be a contiguous verbatim span of the request covering >= 50% of its non-whitespace characters — a multi-payload case commits a `handover` span and is graded by containment instead (evals/task-intake/properties.py _golden_handover); it does NOT check that the instruction sentence was stripped (a hand-over of the whole request passes, decoy payload included), does not check that the RIGHT span was chosen when a request holds two candidate payloads, and does not grade the downstream agent's result.

Policy is house policy, not ground truth: a bare email with no instruction is email-triage; 'reply/answer/write back' is reply-draft even on a newsletter (instruction wins); a bare call transcript is transcript-en. A different shop would label some of these differently; the exam measures adherence to THIS policy as stated in prompt.md.

7 'none' cases in the first 38 (9 of 46), 3 of them baits that name a client, a document or an email; a model that dispatches every request somewhere is caught by those, a model that abstains on everything is caught by the other 31.

Heavy band (8 cases, 2026-09-05): added because the first 38 saturated at the top (2B and 4B both 16/16 heldout, 21/22 train); their split was assigned at authoring, before any model ran them, and ratified with the rest at merge.
